The test uses a typical vertex (0) and a negative weight, but does not exercise explicit boundary values (e.g., zero weight, Integer.MAX_VALUE, min/max vertices). No empty/zero/negative boundary combinations are systematically tested.

No helper methods or constants are used to encapsulate repeated setup. Although the single test is short, there is no modularization (no private helper or constants) to improve reuse and maintainability.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The method is small, has a simple linear flow with no loops or complex conditionals, and is well within the recommended size (<20 lines).

The test contains multiple specific assertions verifying several properties of the returned Aresta and the graph (origin, destination, weight, and vertex count), which improves fault detection beyond superficial checks.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out @Test methods visible. The test is active and runnable (annotated with @Test(timeout=4000)).
The test and class do not include annotations or comments that map the test to a requirement ID or ticket (no @Story, @Requirement, or REQ-/JIRA- tags are present in the method).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes a @Test(timeout = 4000) which is an explicit timing constraint; therefore the presence of a timeout indicates performance-conscious testing at the unit level per the evaluation rules.
The method name 'test8' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. It lacks a descriptive naming pattern like methodName_condition_expectedResult.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method name 'test8' and the comment indicating preservation from a generated class, plus unused EvoSuite-related imports in the class header, are signals of auto-generated tests and naming. This suggests generation artifacts remain.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes Given/When/Then comments that explicitly structure the scenario, indicating thoughtfulness in test design and intent consistent with BDD/Given-When-Then structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public APIs (Grafo constructor, insereAresta, proxAdj) and does not access private fields or use reflection, reducing brittleness tied to implementation details.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals with expected/actual) and include descriptive failure messages for many checks, rather than relying on generic assertTrue/assertNotNull only.
The test uses minimal and useful comments (Given/When/Then) that explain the scenario rather than code mechanics; there are no excessive or commented-out code blocks.
No sources of non-determinism (randomness, current time, Thread.sleep, external systems) are present; the test uses deterministic local state and operations.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only uses local in-memory objects and does not persist data, alter static state, or create external resources that require cleanup. No @After cleanup is necessary based on visible code.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization that enables selective execution. The label is meaningful for unit tests.

PRINCIPLE: Each test case must focus on a single requirement/behavior (single Arrange-Act-Assert).
RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make failures easy to diagnose and avoid masking other failures.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if exactly one Act operation or one clear Arrange-Act-Assert block; non-compliant if multiple Acts or multiple unrelated scenarios are present.
DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations. 2) Check test name for multiple operations. 3) If only one method call and one assertion group -> compliant.
VERDICT: The method constructs two Grafo instances (new Grafo(628) and new Grafo(0)) and asserts both, representing two Act operations / two scenarios in the same test. According to rule 1 this is multiple Acts -> non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests or execution order, and use setup/teardown if needed.
RATIONALE: Independence enables flexible execution order and parallel runs.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only local variables or proper @Before/@After; non-compliant if shared mutable state used without reset.
DECISION RULES: 1) Check for @Before/@After. 2) Check for modified static/instance variables. 3) If only local variables used, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The test uses only local variables (grafoTypical, grafoZero) and no shared mutable state is visible. No evidence of inter-test dependencies -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: For each method under test, provide at least a happy path and an error scenario.
RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and correct handling of exceptional inputs.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when test class includes both success and exception tests (e.g., @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows) for the method under test.
DECISION RULES: 1) If all tests only use valid inputs and expect success, mark non-compliant. 2) Look for @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows. 3) If class has < 2 test methods total, mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: The class contains a single test method. Although it asserts normal (628) and zero (0) scenarios in the same method, there is no explicit test for an exceptional/error condition (e.g., negative size or illegal argument). Per the decision rules (class has <2 test methods and no exception test) -> non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate inputs at boundaries (min, max, zero, negative, etc.).
RATIONALE: Boundary cases often reveal off-by-one and range errors.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when tests include empty/zero/negative or min/max values or names indicate boundary tests.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for empty string, 0, -1, Integer.MAX_VALUE. 2) Look for method names with 'zero', 'min', etc.
VERDICT: The test explicitly constructs a Grafo with size 0 and asserts numVertices == 0, which is a boundary value. Therefore this practice is satisfied -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained; repeated setup should be extracted into helpers/constants.
RATIONALE: Modularity reduces duplication and improves maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if helper methods or constants are used or if tests are short (<10 lines) and don't repeat code.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for private helper methods or constants. 2) If tests are very short and don't repeat code, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The test is short and self-contained without repeated blocks across multiple methods (only one method present). No duplication visible -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and avoid loops/complex conditionals.
RATIONALE: Low complexity reduces risk of test bugs and improves readability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if methods <20 lines and contain no loops or nested conditionals.
DECISION RULES: 1) If any method >30 lines mark non-compliant. 2) If loops or complex conditionals exist mark non-compliant. 3) If methods <15 lines and simple, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The method is short (well under 20 lines) and contains no loops or conditionals -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive to detect faults, verifying multiple properties where applicable.
RATIONALE: Superficial assertions can pass despite incorrect behavior.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests contain multiple meaningful assertions (>=2) or verify multiple properties of objects/collections.
DECISION RULES: 1) If only 1 assertion (especially assertNotNull/assertTrue) mark non-compliant. 2) If tests verify >=2 properties, mark compliant.
VERDICT: This test contains two specific assertEquals assertions (one per scenario). Overall it contains multiple assertions rather than a single superficial assert -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests; keep tests runnable.
RATIONALE: Ignored or commented tests hide problems and reduce suite value.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test lines exist.
DECISION RULES: 1) Search for @Ignore/@Disabled. 2) Search for commented-out @Test. 3) If none, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The code contains no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out tests -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Each test should be linked to a requirement or ticket via annotations or comments.
RATIONALE: Traceability helps map tests to requirements and aids impact analysis.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Story/@Requirement/@Ticket annotations or Javadoc with REQ-/US- IDs are present.
DECISION RULES: 1) Search for @Story/@Requirement/@Ticket. 2) Search for REQ-/US-/JIRA- IDs in Javadoc. 3) If none present, mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: The test and class lack any requirement annotations or Javadoc markers (no REQ-/US- IDs). The class comment mentions a requirement reference in prose but no explicit traceability identifiers are present -> non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Performance and security must be tested explicitly when relevant; use timeouts for performance unit tests.
RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements can be critical; timeouts detect regressions in performance.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if explicit performance tests exist (e.g., @Test(timeout=...) or timing assertions) or security tests are present.
DECISION RULES: 1) Usually not-applicable for unit tests. 2) Mark compliant ONLY if explicit performance tests (timeout) or security tests are present.
VERDICT: The test method uses @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit performance-related assertion (execution must complete within the time bound). Therefore this practice is satisfied -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome (e.g., method_condition_expectedResult).
RATIONALE: Descriptive names make tests self-documenting and help diagnose failures quickly.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test names follow descriptive conventions; non-compliant if names are generic like test1, test6.
DECISION RULES: 1) If name follows methodName_condition_result pattern -> compliant. 2) If names are generic (test6) -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: The method name 'test6' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected behavior (despite inline comments). Per decision rule 2 this is non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Generated tests should be minimal and focused; avoid verbose auto-generated artifacts.
RATIONALE: Large autogenerated tests are hard to maintain; minimal generated tests are preferable.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if auto-generated comments or repetitive test names (test0, test1) appear; not-applicable if no indications of generation.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for 'Auto-generated by...' comments. 2) Look for repetitive test names. 3) If no signs of generation, mark not-applicable.
VERDICT: Although class comment mentions preservation of original generated names, there are no explicit auto-generated comments such as 'Auto-generated by...' nor repetitive generated patterns beyond a single generic name. Based on the decision rules this practice is not-applicable (no clear signs of heavy code generation).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD-style names, TDD/BDD patterns).
RATIONALE: Test-first design or clear structure increases coverage and maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if Given-When-Then comments, BDD naming or comprehensive scenarios are present.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming. 2) If tests cover multiple scenarios, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The test includes explicit 'Given & When' and 'Then' comments indicating structured design intent, which satisfies the practice -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on observable behavior through public APIs, not internal implementation details.
RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are more robust to refactoring and reduce maintenance.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests call public methods and avoid reflection or checking private fields.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for reflection usage; if none and only public API called, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The test uses the public Grafo constructor and public numVertices() method; no reflection or internal state checking -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use specific assertions with descriptive messages to detect subtle faults.
RATIONALE: Specific assertions and messages make test failures easier to diagnose.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions use assertEquals/assertThat and include descriptive messages rather than generic assertTrue.
DECISION RULES: 1) If assertions include messages and use specific methods, mark compliant. 2) If frequent use of assertTrue when assertEquals is better, mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: The test uses assertEquals with descriptive messages for both assertions (specific assertions) -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' not 'what'; avoid excessive or outdated comments.
RATIONALE: Useful comments clarify complex logic while avoiding clutter.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if code is clean with minimal helpful comments; non-compliant if commented-out code or excessive comments are present.
DECISION RULES: 1) If commented-out code present, mark non-compliant. 2) If >50% of lines are comments, mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: The test contains concise Given/When/Then comments and no commented-out code or excessive commentary -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid sources of non-determinism (random, time, external dependencies) unless controlled/mocked.
RATIONALE: Deterministic tests avoid flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no Random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep(), or external dependencies without mocking.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for Random(), current time, Thread.sleep(). 2) If absent and test uses local deterministic values, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The test uses fixed literal sizes (628, 0) and no random/time/external dependencies -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests must not modify shared state or leave persistent artifacts; use cleanup when needed.
RATIONALE: Side effects produce inter-test dependencies and flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only local variables and no persistent resources; non-compliant if they create files/databases without cleanup.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @After with cleanup. 2) Look for file/database creation without cleanup. 3) If only local variables are used and no persistence, mark compliant.
VERDICT: The test only creates local Grafo instances and does not persist data or modify static state -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Use @Tag/@Category to organize tests for selective execution.
RATIONALE: Labels improve CI efficiency and test management.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Tag/@Category annotations are present and meaningful.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @Tag/@Category. 2) If present and meaningful, mark compliant; otherwise non-compliant.
VERDICT: The test class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing meaningful categorization -> compliant.
